scope: Replace the advisory validate endpoint's separate read and ownedIds Python bridge calls with one validationContext call. Keep every fresh isolated JVM, BuildIdentity hash fence, existing sandbox resource/exit/reaping rule, whole-module/parser validation and public response identity. No outcome/context/authority cache, persisted schema, index, solver/JIT/GC flag, worker protocol, durable mutation or browser behavior change.
normative_amendment: Only the new read-only validationContext store operation uses REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY. Existing mutation/read/ownedIds methods retain their existing READ COMMITTED behavior. Every SQL statement, transaction control and scope setup still traverses canonical sql_connections and the pinned SQLeanParser proxy. No change to parser allowlists is proposed: exact SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY is already admitted and tested.

implementation_boundary.java: DocumentQueries.validate collects the exact existing server-ID set, performs one validationContext call, validates its closed reply and passes artifact/inventory to the unchanged fresh DocumentWorker. New encapsulated helper(s) may carry context parsing/ID extraction to keep every callable <=30 physical lines with full meaningful Javadoc. No shared worker or mutable cache. DocumentGateway/FrameProcess/DocumentWorker/BubblewrapLauncher resource and identity behavior stays unchanged.
implementation_boundary.python: Add CLI SHAPES/dispatch validationContext and Store.validation_context with a dedicated snapshot context manager. Reuse _read and collect_ids semantics. A factored history collector may be shared with legacy owned_ids only if all existing behavior/tests remain unchanged; do not alter legacy transaction isolation or expose a connection supplied by the browser.
implementation_boundary.sql: Existing schema/RLS/grants/quotas remain. Only existing SELECT queries plus the already permitted transaction-mode command are used. No SQL string interpolation from request fields.
implementation_boundary.formal: Candidate-only ValidationContext.lean and exact actual #check inventory; 287 inherited propositions unchanged. No active import/spec until six exact-model council approvals and two registered clean builds.
implementation_boundary.excluded_candidate: The rejected reusable-JVM package at gates/document/validator-session-candidate remains immutable and inactive; none of its classloader/image/lifecycle proposals are bundled here.

private_request.outer: Existing closed protocol1 envelope {protocol,requestId,operation,args}; operation exactly validationContext; canonical UUID requestId generated by Java and echoed by CLI. Existing duplicate-key/UTF8/scalar/nesting/unknown-field rejection applies.

args.documentId: server-derived route document; canonical server: UUID accepted by existing wire.identifier, not CREATE
args.revision: explicit baseRevision, type integer excluding Boolean, 0..9007199254740991 inclusive; never null/current-head selector
args.ids: deduplicated ascending lexicographically ordered array of at most4096 canonical server identifiers; reject duplicate, unsorted, malformed or non-string IDs in this new private operation

private_request.extraction: Traverse the current candidate.module exactly as existing DocumentQueries.inventory: visit array/object values, collect every textual value starting server:, deduplicate and sort. SOURCE or absent module yields empty set; no arbitrary candidate/source text is interpreted as authority. Names, draft IDs and client type flags never establish ownership. Malformed module/type checking still belongs to the independent worker; extraction is not validation.
private_request.bounds: Encoded args <=262144 UTF8 bytes; complete private frame remains <3145728 bytes. Existing public HTTP body<=262144 and inherited nesting/source/graph limits remain. The added revision field counts toward the args bound. Bound before spawning a bridge.
private_request.scope: No principal/workspace/logical-launch/bearer/connection/isolation fields allowed. Store derives private scope from existing immutable metadata. Document ownership is principal/workspace/document; logicalLaunch partitions receipts, not retained document history.

sequence: Open exactly one canonical allow-app connection through sql_connections, with normal autocommit=false behavior. Psycopg emits BEGIN through the same proxy; do not rely on SET outside a transaction.
As the first explicit application statement, before any SELECT including set_config, execute exact SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY.
Apply existing transaction-local allow.tenant,allow.project,allow.purpose settings via the three bound-parameter SELECT set_config statements. No table read occurs until all settings succeeded.
Read exact document head and requested immutable revision/artifact with existing _read queries. Missing/foreign document and absent base fail closed without data.

If requested IDs are nonempty, scan ALL artifacts for the same document inside this SAME transaction/snapshot using existing SELECT content and collect_ids logic. Scan continues after all IDs found so later collisions cannot be hidden. Empty IDs require no history scan and return empty object.

Form the closed context response from the snapshot. Exit transaction successfully and close connection BEFORE returning data to the CLI/Java and before launching Alloy. Any query/decode/transaction-exit failure discards the complete result. No worker process or external solver runs inside SQL transaction.
snapshot_protocol.visibility: All data queries observe the snapshot selected by PostgreSQL at the first non-transaction-control statement; this may be the first set_config SELECT. A commit after that point is excluded from head, base and inventory together. A commit before it is visible together subject to RLS. This is an observation at one instant, not a promise of latest head at response time or SERIALIZABLE transaction scheduling.
snapshot_protocol.concurrent_commit: An accepted historical base remains usable when head later advances. IDs introduced in history after base but visible in this snapshot may be returned, matching existing owned-history semantics. IDs introduced by a commit after the snapshot remain absent; request may be rejected by fresh worker and a later ordinary retry obtains a new snapshot. Do not mix a newer inventory/head into an older snapshot or reread missing IDs in another transaction.
snapshot_protocol.head_observed: headObserved is the head in the same snapshot, integer>=revision. It is private informational evidence only. It is never used for expected-revision CAS, mutation authority, head replacement, browser accepted state or analysis freshness; it is not passed as a checked candidate token. Public validation reply remains unchanged.
snapshot_protocol.locking: No FOR UPDATE/SHARE and no workspace/document/admission row locks in this read-only path. MVCC snapshot replaces the need to block commits. Existing mutating workspace->document->admission lock order and READ COMMITTED transactions remain untouched.
snapshot_protocol.auth: HTTP authentication/readiness/current worker permit remain mandatory per call. SQL RLS establishes current scoped document visibility at this transaction; a reused process/result is never authorization. Administrative restore, schema/RLS/grant changes remain inherited trusted maintenance operations and are not concurrent app APIs.

inventory.definition_source: Only definitions found by existing Store.collect_ids in immutable artifacts visible for this principal/workspace/document snapshot. Preserve existing kind mapping: signature,field,predicate,fact,assertion,command,binder,expression. References/arbitrary strings alone do not create returned definitions. TEXT_ONLY module=null contributes no IDs.
inventory.completeness: For every requested ID, return its unique historical kind iff at least one visible artifact definition has that ID. Same ID/kind repeated over history collapses to one entry. Unrequested IDs never appear. Missing or foreign IDs remain absent and cannot be recategorized as fresh draft identities.
inventory.conflicts: A requested ID found with different kinds anywhere in visible history fails the complete operation. No first-match/last-match overwrite, early-return after all requested IDs found, silently skipped malformed artifacts or partial inventory.
inventory.response_checks: Java validates every returned map key is in its exact requested set and every value is one allowed kind string. The trusted SQL adapter supplies completeness; browser-provided map/checked flag is never consumed. Existing IdentityRemapper performs fresh whole-candidate ownership/kind checking; this read does not authorize commit.

private_response.correspondence: Success status is existing OK only after the complete snapshot transaction exited. documentId and baseRevision equal exact private request. headObserved>=baseRevision and all revisions fit the safe integer bound. artifact is the same decoded immutable artifact object returned by existing _read, retaining exact source string/hash, field order, occurrence/trivia/descriptor content and stored policy/dependency fields. Transport JSON key ordering need not equal original stored JSON bytes; source bytes/content identity are preserved. Do not relabel a historical artifact policy as current.
private_response.shape: Exactly these five fields, no provenance/current-head/authority/cache fields. artifact is an object with the existing exact ARTIFACT_FIELDS shape; ownedIdInventory an object. Java rejects missing,extra,wrong-type,mismatched-document/base,invalid head or foreign inventory field before starting worker. Fresh ArtifactIntegrity/parser remains authoritative for content semantics.
private_response.bounds: Complete serialized CLI envelope <=1572864 bytes excluding final newline; Java capture remains1572865 including framing. Exact artifact limit1MiB and inventory/request bounds stay. Count the whole encoded envelope, not sums of guessed components; oversized output emits existing bounded UNAVAILABLE and no partial context. Existing private worker frame remains<2MiB and complete worker/public output<=1MiB.
private_response.failure: Malformed arguments/store missing data retain existing ERROR classification; DB/proxy/decoder/transaction transport failures return UNAVAILABLE through existing CLI conventions. Java treats every non-OK or malformed context as IOException/unavailability and starts no worker. Read-only context failures never create UNKNOWN_COMMIT_OUTCOME or known-write-rollback claims; existing mutator uncertainty handling remains untouched.

resources.bridge: Exactly one one-shot private Python child for validationContext, retaining 2GiB address space,20CPU seconds,20-second external wall deadline, bounded stdout/stderr and unconditional reap. No connection pool/background process introduced.
resources.worker: After successful context and bridge exit, same new DocumentWorker per request with full constructor/launch BuildIdentity scans, pinned Alloy check,512MiB heap,2GiBAS,12CPU seconds,10s external wall,existing shared principal/global capacity and zero validation queue. No JIT/GC/JVM flags change.
resources.history: Existing workspace quotas remain64documents,4096revisions,16384receipts,256MiB accounted payload; no retention deletion. The scan remains the existing authorized complete-history traversal. These payload quotas are not heap/RSS guarantees. Existing process AS/CPU/wall caps fail closed if a permitted large history cannot be processed. No unbounded accumulating decoded artifact list; decode/collect one artifact at a time, retain only base artifact/requested-ID map/current cursor result as existing driver semantics allow. Psycopg client cursor buffering must be measured and disclosed, not called server streaming.
resources.quota_full: This read reserves no quota, increments no counters and remains readable at logical quota exhaustion, subject to existing physical availability/output bounds. No quota reservation/cache or durable admission is created.
resources.publication: Worker starts only after successful full context transaction and bridge exit; interruption holds existing permit until every started child is reaped. Public stale-response/requestHash guards unchanged.

idempotency_and_nonmutation.advisory: There is no idempotency key or receipt for validationContext. Repeating the same read may observe a newer committed snapshot. Exact immutable base content is stable; headObserved/inventory may expand. No hidden retry inside one bridge after snapshot failure. HTTP caller may perform ordinary new advisory requests.
idempotency_and_nonmutation.durable: Read-only operation cannot append artifact/revision/receipt, update head/title, reserve/release quota, rotate owner nonce, finalize or recover admission. Fresh commit/history/analysis paths independently reread/revalidate exactly as before; context reply is never accepted there as authority.

formal.mechanism: Actual Lean #check output captures full printed types for each exact proposition; never truncate source text at := because structure updates may contain :=. Source SHA and complete output must match both independent clean builds. Concrete witness includes revision0 and CRLF source.
formal.modeled: Finite scoped snapshot read, requested/historical inventory membership and completeness, collision rejection/unique kind, exact base/head, wrong scope/document/future/missing base denial, read nonmutation, fixed-snapshot concurrency and immutable append preservation.
formal.trusted_or_tested: PostgreSQL16 MVCC snapshot/isolation/RLS, driver BEGIN ordering, SQLeanParser and wire parsing, Store.collect_ids extraction, exact Java/JSON identity checks, process isolation/budgets, source/artifact runtime correspondence and canonical solver semantics. The model does not prove these adapters; finite runtime tests plus inherited TCB declarations provide their evidence.
